newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Land Secs raises profits, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Land Secs raises profits, sees growth.

text.p: British property giant Land Securities Plc, whose portfolio is valued at 5.76 billion pounds ($9.5 billion), on Wednesday announced a 2.6 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 243.8 million pounds in the year to March 31.
It posted a 13.3 percent rise in net asset value per share to 783p from 691p and its managing director Sir Peter Hunt told Reuters he sees continued steady growth in rental income from prime sites.
"It's still a fact that rental growth is patchy but it's nice to see a bit of a return to growth, a bit of demand and values gently increasing," Hunt said in an interview.

Land Securities shares rose sharply to reach a high of 880p before settling 31.5 higher at 875.5 in a generally strong property sector where interest rate-sensitive shares were boosted by the lack of a rate rise in the United States on Tuesday.
Land's shares were also helped by the fact that its profits were above the top end of market forecasts which went as high as 240 million pounds.
Hunt said that in the retail sector, the major growth areas were in out of town shopping centres and retail warehouses while in city centres, there was also growth in prime sites.
"But the high street is shortening," commented Hunt, pointing out that there was little or no growth in sites away from the centre.
He said that the market had continued in a similar vein in the current financial year since March 31.
"We've continued to do deals at satisfactory rents, there's a little bit of growth," he said.

Hunt announced he would be retiring as managing director of the company on his 65th birthday on July 1, 1998 when he will be succeeded by his current deputy Ian Henderson. Hunt will remain as chairman.

In his statement accompanying the results, Hunt said that the recent change in government in Britain did cause some uncertainty but called for policies that would create confidence and stimulate the property market.

He told Reuters he expected the Labour government to follow broadly similar policies to those pursued by its predecessor although uncertainty over its fiscal stance meant that the path of growth in the economy would be uncertain for a while.
On the question of the new government's attitude to town planning Hunt said, "I'm ever hopeful that they will pursue the same policies."
In the City of London financial district, Land said the encouraging increase in the level of occupational enquiries had continued in the past year. ($ = 0.604 British Pounds)
